title: Compliance Warden: policy-as-code sentinel with auto-remediation and evidence bundling for residency & retention
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood needs an automated, auditable system to ensure customer-configured residency and retention policies are continuously enforced across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. Current gaps: policy changes can drift from source-of-truth (Terraform/console), alerts are noisy and manual remediation is slow, and evidence packaging for audits is ad hoc.

Goal:
Build a Compliance Warden service that evaluates policy-as-code (OPA + Rego) against live configuration, detects configuration drift for data residency and retention settings, performs safe remediation where allowed, and produces tamper-evident evidence bundles for audits. The system should support:
- policy authoring pull from existing policy repo (git),
- periodic + event-driven evaluation,
- drift classification (intentional change vs drift),
- automated remediation playbooks with canary + dry-run modes,
- evidence collection and canonicalization for export to customer audit stores.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement UI console surfaces (Console task will be a follow-up),
- Does not replace infra-level enforcement for platform-owned controls (we will call into existing infra agents).

Success metrics:
- Mean time to detect policy drift < 10 minutes for critical residency rules (after relevant config/event),
- Automated remediation applied successfully for >= 80% of non-blocking drift cases in staging,
- Evidence bundle generation time < 60s and verified by CI signature check,
- False positive alert rate < 5% in a 2-week pilot on 50 tenants.

Design overview:
1) Policy ingestion: watch a git repo (policy-as-code) and surface policy versions. Integrate with OPA/Rego evaluation engine and maintain a policy catalog with metadata (scope: customer, org, global; enforceability level: audit-only/auto-remediate).
2) Discovery & snapshot: scheduled and event-driven snapshotting of effective configs (control-plane API + telemetry hooks). Snapshots are hashed and stored in a versioned evidence store (S3 with object immutability + KMS).
3) Drift detector: comparator service that runs policy evaluations against snapshots, classifies diff by severity and origin (human-initiated vs unknown drift). Use sequence numbers and operator audit logs to infer intentional changes.
4) Remediation orchestrator: for policies marked auto-remediate, run safe remediation steps: dry-run -> canary -> full apply. Support rollback hooks and require signed approvals for high-severity remediation. Remediations are executed through existing platform agents (calls to infra reconciler).
5) Evidence bundler: assemble signed evidence artifact containing: evaluated policy version, snapshot diff, remediation audit log, and system state identifiers. Provide export in compressed JSONL with SHA256 manifest and envelope signed by platform KMS key.
6) Observability: per-policy dashboards (drift rate, remediation success, MTTR), alerting rules, incident links, and a compliance telemetry feed for Console and Security teams.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline working in staging for 3 sample policies (residency: tenant-region-lock, retention: message-retention-days, retention: session-kv-ttl).
- Evidence bundle produced and validated by audit CI job (signature + manifest checksum).
- A remediation playbook for retention TTL implemented with canary mode and rollback tested in staging.
- Unit + integration tests for detector + orchestrator with >= 90% coverage for critical paths.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: PoC policy ingestion and OPA evaluation harness, sample policies ported; storage schema for snapshots and bundles.
- Week 2: Drift detector service and classifier; basic dashboard wireframe; integrate with snapshotter.
- Week 3: Remediation orchestrator MVP (dry-run + canary) hooking into infra reconciler; implement audit log plumbing.
- Week 4: Evidence bundler + KMS signing; CI validation; staging pilot with 10 tenants.
- Week 5: Hardening, metrics/alerts, security review, prepare rollout plan for broader pilot.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: auto-remediation could cause customer-visible disruption. Mitigation: default to audit-only for high-risk policies, require signed approvals for remediation, and implement canary/dry-run safeguards.
- Risk: high volume of snapshots causes storage costs. Mitigation: incremental diffs and retention policy for evidence with tiered storage.
- Risk: policy mismatch across platform versions. Mitigation: include policy version matrix and compatibility checks during ingestion.

Notes for reviewers:
- The PoC uses OPA for policy evaluation; we should validate performance with 10k snapshot evaluations/min. If OPA doesn't scale, we'll evaluate embedding evaluation into the runtime.
- Need product/Console alignment for how evidence bundles will be surfaced to customers (S3 + signed URL vs Console export).

Next steps:
- Sync with Security (scheduled 2025-02-19) for KMS signing and audit requirements,
- Create follow-up Console ticket to add a per-tenant policy status page and evidence download UX,
- Begin integration with infra reconciler team for safe remediation APIs.
